result.title: Pandora's Toolbox Or Why Agent Safety Cannot Be Verified
result.summary: Present artificial intelligence agents are constructed by means of a coupling between a fixed language model with a general computing device. We show that this coupling makes safety undecidable. In particular, we show that given some dangerous program, no algorithm can predict whether an agent will run such a program that is semantically equivalent. In general, guardrails, blacklists, whitelists and certifications can only lead to imperfect safety solutions. Under finite constraints (bounded context, values and running time) safety is decidable but still intractable. Specifically, the problem is $\mathsf{PSPACE}$-complete even when the description of the agent is known. Finally, safety is not a compositional property, i.e., agents that can be proven safe on their own can still produce unsafe behavior when grouped together. We also discuss relaxed notions of safety that could be used in practice.

AI.brief_summary: 论文从可计算性角度论证：语言模型与通用计算设备耦合而成的智能体，其安全性判定不可判定；在上下文、取值与运行时间受限时可判定但仍为 PSPACE 完全，且安全性不具组合性，并讨论了实践中可用的宽松安全定义。
AI.relevance_reason: 该文不涉及多模态表示或 latent 生成，但其关于行为验证的可判定性与组合性边界，可能为「latent 推理是否真正使用视觉证据」这类过程验证目标提供理论类比，具体可迁移程度需核查。
